newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Premier says Russian economic reforms will go on.
newsitem.headline: Premier says Russian economic reforms will go on.

text.p: Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Friday there was no question of a reversal of Russian economic reforms despite President Boris Yeltsin's absence through illness.

"The West should not worry. Reforms are not stopping, it's just that we don't have much money. But the desire (to reform) is great," Chernomyrdin told reporters. "There have been reforms and there will be reforms. There will be no U-turns in Russia."
Many economists say reforms have slowed during Yeltsin's absences through illness this year and last year, but Chernomyrdin said there was no reason to worry.

The prime minister, a former gas industry chief, has taken on the role as the main guarantor of Russian economic reforms. He stood in for Yeltsin while the president underwent open heart surgery in November last year.

Yeltsin, who turns 66 on February 1, was taken ill again earlier this month and he has been receiving treatment in hospital for pneumonia for just over a week. Doctors said on Thursday that his condition had "stabilised significantly".
